title: Talent Agency Cosmic Opens London Office, Led by Gabrielle de Cevins
description: Cosmic Talents, which represents leading international heads of department, is opening a London office. It will be led by Gabrielle de Cevins, who j
body:
Cosmic Talents, which represents leading international heads of department, is opening a London office. It will be led by Gabrielle de Cevins, who joins Cosmic Talents as the agency’s U.K.-based agent.

	De Cevins brings eight years of in-house production experience to the role, including the last four at London-based feature film production company The Bureau (“Queen at Sea,” “Black Church Bay,” “A Long Winter”), and will oversee representation of the agency’s roster of directors of photography, production designers, costume designers and editors across the U.K. market for both features and commercials.
	

	She will work hand in hand with Paris-based agents Marie Berg, Elodie Vongdara and Andréa Bernard.


	In recent years, the agency’s talent have been responsible for the cinematography of films such as Edward Berger’s “Conclave” (Stéphane Fontaine), Magnus von Horn’s “The Girl With the Needle” (Michal Dymek) and Andrey Zvyagintsev’s “Minotaur” (Mikhail Krichman).

	Berg, managing director and agent at Cosmic Talents, said, “The U.K. market is exceptionally creative. Its directors and the stories they tell are a constant source of inspiration. By opening this office, we want to strengthen our presence in the U.K. and establish a deeper connection with this vibrant creative community.

	“Having a local representative brings greater spontaneity to our relationships and allows us to build meaningful connections with directors, clients and production partners.

	“With a background in production, Gabrielle has a strong understanding of the realities and challenges of producing in the U.K. Her experience enables her to bridge creative ambitions with the practical demands of production, making her ideally positioned to support projects in this market.”
	

	De Cevins said, “I’m delighted to be joining a team with such a strong commitment to artistic vision. Cosmic has built an exceptional roster over the years. I’m looking forward to helping production find the right creative partners for their projects, and to championing Cosmic talents within the U.K. market.”

schema.headline: Talent Agency Cosmic Opens London Office, Led by Gabrielle de Cevins

title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor Taking Legal Action Against Police Over Search Warrants in Arrest
description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, the former prince and King Charles’ brother, is taking legal action against the Thames Valley Police over search warrant
body:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, the former prince and King Charles’ brother, is taking legal action against the Thames Valley Police over search warrants relating to his February arrest.

	As first reported by The Telegraph, Mountbatten-Windsor — who was arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office after the release of the Epstein files — has submitted a judicial review regarding the search warrants that allowed the police to investigate his Sandringham Estate home and former residence at the Royal Lodge in Windsor. 
	

	“We are engaged in legal proceedings in relation to warrants previously obtained from the Central Criminal Court,” the Thames Valley Police confirmed to BBC News. “As these legal proceedings are currently ongoing, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further.” 


	A private court hearing will be held on Thursday to consider Mountbatten-Windsor’s request. 

	Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested by the Thames Valley Police on Feb. 19, his 66th birthday, in relation to their investigation into a a complaint that alleged the former prince had shared confidential material with the late, disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein. He was later released under investigation.

	Mountbatten-Windsor was stripped of his royal title last year over his ties to Epstein, and was mentioned and pictured many times in the over 3 million pages of the Epstein files, which were released by the U.S. Department of Justice in February. The former prince, who had a longtime friendship with Epstein and maintained contact with him after his 2008 conviction of procuring a child for prostitution, has previously apologized and denied any wrongdoing.
	

	In a statement following Mountbatten-Windsor’s arrest, King Charles said: “I have learned with the deepest concern the news about Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and suspicion of misconduct in public office. What now follows is the full, fair and proper process by which this issue is investigated in the appropriate manner and by the appropriate authorities. In this, as I have said before, they have our full and wholehearted support and co-operation. Let me state clearly: the law must take its course. As this process continues, it would not be right for me to comment further on this matter. Meanwhile, my family and I will continue in our duty and service to you all.”

schema.headline: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor Taking Legal Action Against Police Over Search Warrants in Arrest

title: China Box Office: Crime Procedural ‘Traces of Justice’ Leads National Day Frame
description: New Classics Pictures’ crime procedural drama “Traces of Justice” took the top spot at the mainland China box office during the Oct. 2–4 weekend, gr
body:
New Classics Pictures’ crime procedural drama “Traces of Justice” took the top spot at the mainland China box office during the Oct. 2–4 weekend, grossing RMB208.9 million ($31.2 million) over the three-day frame, according to data from Artisan Gateway. 

	Following its Oct. 1 release to launch the Golden Week holiday corridor, the feature, also known as “Sherlock of China,” has amassed $41.8 million. Directed by Chen Sicheng (“Detective Chinatown”) and co-written with Ji Zhang, the production stars Zhang Yi alongside Li Ma, Li Xuejian, Karry Wang, Fan Chengcheng, and Chen Feiyu. Spanning multiple decades, the period procedural follows a legendary detective who, alongside his dedicated team, cracks complex criminal cases while chronicling the evolving apparatus of China’s public security forces.
	

	Beijing Joy Fun Pictures’ comedy “Mr. & Mrs. Pardon” debuted in second place, pulling in $17.3 million over the weekend frame to lift its cumulative total to $24.5 million since rolling out on Oct. 1. Directed by Shen Chunyang and written by Ma Duo, the satirical family feature stars real-life comedic couple Shen Chunyang and Xiao Shenyang alongside Jia Bing and Yu Yang. The storyline centers on a long-married middle-aged couple grappling with domestic monotony and an escalating marital crisis, whose routine existence descends into slapstick chaos following an unexpected body-swap event.


	Dirty Monkeys’ war comedy-drama “Once Upon a Time in the Middle East” took third position in its eighth weekend, adding $4.4 million to lift its cumulative haul to a massive $349.9 million since its Aug. 11 rollout. Directed by Wen Muye and starring Shen Teng, Jiang Qiming, Aarif Rahman, and Omar Sherif, the enduring summer hit tracks a Chinese chef whose overseas restaurant in a fictional Middle Eastern city becomes a vital civilian refuge following the outbreak of armed conflict.
	

	Pearl Studio’s animated fantasy comedy “All Wishes Come True!” placed fourth in its 12th weekend, collecting $4.3 million. Directed by Mu Zhengyang, the release crossed the RMB2 billion milestone with a cume of $302.2 million since its July 18 premiere.

	Rounding out the top five, CMC Pictures’ crime action thriller sequel “Go for Broke 2” debuted with $4.2 million across its two-day opening frame. Including preview screenings since launching on Oct. 3, the title has accumulated $4.2 million. Written and directed by Marc Ma (“Go for Broke”), the gritty revenge actioner stars Isabella Leong, Wen Junhui (of K-pop boy band Seventeen), and martial arts icon Sammo Hung in a story following a bereaved mother who aligns with another grieving parent to track down a ruthless criminal syndicate responsible for victimizing children.

	Mainland China’s overall weekend box office reached $74.1 million as theatrical activity accelerated for the National Day holiday. Year-to-date box office revenue stands at $4.52 billion, down 29.7% compared to the same period in 2025.

schema.headline: China Box Office: Crime Procedural ‘Traces of Justice’ Leads National Day Frame

title: France’s Canal+ Threatens to Pull $1.1 Billion Cinema Deal Over French Tax Hike
description: Canal+ Group chairman Maxime Saada has warned that the pay TV banner could pull out of its €1 billion ($1.1 billion) investment deal with the French
body:
Canal+ Group chairman Maxime Saada has warned that the pay TV banner could pull out of its €1 billion ($1.1 billion) investment deal with the French film industry if the government goes ahead with plans to double VAT on pay-TV subscriptions.

	The measure, included in the government’s proposed finance bill, would scrap the reduced 10% VAT rate currently applied to subscription-based services and bring it in line with France’s standard 20% rate. Canal+, by far the country’s biggest pay-TV operator and one of the main pillars of French film financing, would be hit hardest, representing a cost of approximately €200 million a year.
	

	The suggested reform come as the French government is under pressure to bring down the country’s growing debt, and is looking for €43 billion in savings and additional revenue in 2027.


	Saada said during an interview with French radio RTL that the change would effectively void Canal+’s existing agreement with French film organizations, under which the group has committed to invest roughly €1 billion in in French and European films between 2028 and 2032.

	“We invest more in cinema than any other player. Our commitment to film organizations is a contract, and the first clause – the quid pro quo for Canal+’s funding of cinema — is the reduced VAT rate,” Saada said. “We don’t even need to renegotiate it. The contract is void if the standard VAT rate is applied.”

	If Canal+ were to fall back on its strict regulatory obligations rather than maintain its current commitments, its annual contribution to cinema could drop to around €50 million, according to Saada. 
	

	“We cannot find ourselves in a situation where we’ll lose €200 million in France. My concern is the group’s long-term viability,” said the Paris-based executive. 

	The pay TV group was behind six movies that played at Cannes this year, notably Quentin Dupieux’s “Full Phil” starring Kristen Stewart and Woody Harrelson, and Jeanne Herry’s “Garance” starring Adèle Exarchopoulos. 

	Canal+ has long argued that its heavy investment in French cinema goes hand in hand with the regulatory and tax advantages afforded to the group. Saada has threatened before to reduce the group’s investment during tense negotiations over windowing rules and Canal+ was granted an earlier access to movies after their theatrical run in exchange for its substantial investment obligations.

	The proposed finance bill also contains a raft of measures affecting public broadcasting. Under the current draft, funding for France’s public broadcasters, mainly France Télévisions, would be cut by €47 million to €3.82 billion. France Televisions’ president Delphine Ernotte Cunci recently said in an interview wiith Le Monde that the pubcaster was also facing €47 million cut in subsidies, along with a 20% decline in advertising revenues, and warned that these cuts represented a “threat to the funding of French cultural production” and exposed the sector’s dependency on U.S. streaming services.

	The bill also proposes reducing by half the tax rebate applied to platforms such as YouTube and TikTok which have benefited from a 66% allowance on advertising revenues since 2016. French film and TV executives have been lobbying hard for YouTube to invest in local content. In the meantime, the change in the levy applied to these services would effectively broaden the tax base and increase hugely the amount flowing into the CNC, the National Film Board which subsidies the cinema and audiovisual industry. 

	The finance bill still has to make its way through the parliament. While the industry braces for budget cuts, it’s also facing threats from Marine Le Pen’s far right party Rassemblement National which is leading polls in the upcoming presidential elections and has been highly critical of French cultural eco-system.

schema.headline: France’s Canal+ Threatens to Pull $1.1 Billion Cinema Deal Over French Tax Hike

title: John Oliver Dodges David Ellison-Skydance News on ‘Last Week Tonight’
description: The big media news this week concerned Skydance Corp., David Ellison’s newly formed Hollywood mega-company comprising Paramount Skydance and Warner
body:
The big media news this week concerned Skydance Corp., David Ellison’s newly formed Hollywood mega-company comprising Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery, which Ellison (and his father Larry) acquired in a $111 billion debt-addled merger that is set to officially close Oct. 6. What the long-term future of the studio behemoth may look like is yet to be determined, though in the immediate it will surely mean massive job cuts and a change in editorial bent for CNN similar to Ellison and Bari Weiss’s CBS News makeover.
	

	It may also mean that John Oliver and “Last Week Tonight” are operating on borrowed time.


	Oliver and his “Last Week Tonight” team extended their contact to 2027 just prior to the merger being finalized, but given how Ellison pulled the plug on Stephen Colbert’s “The Late Show” — presumably at the behest of his political ally, President Trump — who knows if Oliver and co. will make it to the end of the deal.

	And so, on Sunday night, all eyes were on HBO, Oliver and “Last Week Tonight” to see if he’d address Ellison swallowing up his parent company Warner Bros. Discovery. After all, Oliver has poked fun at the Ellisons on the program in the past. The show’s main story covered the history of Secret Service agents’ protection of the U.S. president pegged to the myriad security breaches that have nearly cost Trump his life due to a mixture of incompetence, lack of resources and a “doing more with less” culture. Since the Department of Homeland Security once hired Hollywood filmmaker Michael Bay to shoot a pricey recruitment ad that aired during the Super Bowl, Oliver’s Secret Service segment culminated with a parody ad for the Secret Service featuring Adam DeVine and Anders Holm of “Workaholics” as inept agents.
	

	However, Oliver opted not to address the news that Ellison’s Warner Bros. Discovery takeover had been approved or its rebranding as Skydance Corp.

	Maybe next week?

schema.headline: John Oliver Dodges David Ellison-Skydance News on ‘Last Week Tonight’

title: ‘NAZA’ Rebuttal Doc Surfaces Online, Made by IDF Reserve Members
description: Just as hot-button Gaza documentary “NAZA” — which recently won a special jury prize at the Venice Film Festival — gains international visibility an
body:
Just as hot-button Gaza documentary “NAZA” — which recently won a special jury prize at the Venice Film Festival — gains international visibility and media attention, a counter project has surfaced online titled “NAZA: The Real Story.”

	The original 80-minute doc, which was shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv and explores the killings of Palestinian civilians in Gaza, features revelatory interviews with 24 Israeli military intelligence officers and soldiers. “NAZA,” a term that appears throughout the documentary, is an acronym for collateral damage used by Israeli intelligence to indicate the number of civilians it expects will be killed in an airstrike.
	

	“NAZA,” which was helmed by Israeli directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor — two of the four co-directors of 2025’s Oscar-winning doc “No Other Land” — earned a massive 24.5-minute ovation at Venice and was also well received when it recently bowed in North America at the New York Film Festival. It is currently playing in cinemas in Europe and the U.S. before it will be made visible to stream for free on The Guardian website in late November.


	It is now being countered by the rapidly made 49-minute rebuttal “NAZA: The Real Story,” shot in a style that mimics the original. According to information on its website, the film has been made by Lt. Col. Roi Danino, who is a political candidate for the right-wing Israel First party led by Sharren Haskel in Israel’s upcoming Oct. 27 elections; Ariel Averbuch, a reserve major in the Israel Defense Forces, who is a patent attorney and ultra-nationalist influencer; and content editor Hagai Gutman.
	

	The documentary was reposted on X by the Israeli Embassy to the U.S. on Saturday, which wrote “a new Israeli documentary is setting the record straight” alongside a link to its website.

	According to the “NAZA: The Real Story” website, the rebuttal doc, similarly to the original, describes the war in Gaza as “told through the testimonies of IDF officers who took part.”

	“Through firsthand accounts, this documentary examines combat in civilian areas, the challenges of identifying threats, and the decisions made on the battlefield,” says the blurb on the rebuttal piece’s home page. “Their testimonies offer a closer look at the conditions they faced, the dilemmas they encountered, and how they describe the conduct of the war.”

	“NAZA: The Real Story” argues that “Hamas fought from inside civilian areas: fighters in civilian clothes, weapons in homes, schools, mosques and a hospital, tunnel shafts inside houses. And that the IDF ran its operations under strict rules for opening fire because of it. Those are the film’s claims, made by the people who were there,” according to the website. 

	At publishing time, the “NAZA: The Real Story” website asserts that more than 20 million viewers have already seen the doc that was released online this weekend.

	Last week, the Israeli Defense Forces slammed “NAZA” in a statement, calling it “manipulative,” “misleading” and “based on substantial factual errors.”

	“With the original ‘NAZA’ film gaining heavy distribution and visibility across Europe and the United States, the creators of this rebuttal are utilizing digital influencers and grassroots international networks to push their footage directly to global policymakers and journalists,” wrote the right-wing newspaper Jerusalem Post.

	“For the production team, the ongoing clash is no longer just a debate over military strategy but a definitive, high-stakes war over who dictates the historical record to the international community.”

	There was no comment about “NAZA: The Real Story” from Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and from The Guardian, which produced “NAZA” in tandem with James Wilson (JW Films) and executive producer Jonathan Glazer.

schema.headline: ‘NAZA’ Rebuttal Doc Surfaces Online, Made by IDF Reserve Members

title: Harvey Keitel Plays Acting Teacher in Gaurav Bhardwaj’s Debut Feature ‘The Method’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Harvey Keitel stars as a celebrated acting teacher in “The Method,” the first feature from director and co-writer Gaurav Bhardwaj, produced by “CTRL
body:
Harvey Keitel stars as a celebrated acting teacher in “The Method,” the first feature from director and co-writer Gaurav Bhardwaj, produced by “CTRL” banner Travelin Bone Entertainment alongside Imagination Infinite Motion Pictures.

	Mina Sundwall (“Murdaugh: Death in the Family,” “Lost in Space”) also features, as do Rakshit Bhuchar and Rohan Maletira, both of whom make their feature debuts with the film.


	The story plays out in New York’s cutthroat acting scene, where a talented Indian actor chasing his craft falls under the sway of Keitel’s teacher. As ambition, friendship and artistic ideals pull against one another, the mentor challenges every one of them to consider what they would give up to succeed.
	

	Production has wrapped in the New York and New Jersey area, and the film is expected to release in 2027.

	“‘The Method’ is not simply a film about acting,” said Bhardwaj. “It explores the journeys of four artists: an Indian actor, a Canadian actor, an American playwright and director, and a revered acting teacher portrayed by the legendary actor, Harvey Keitel. At its core, it is a film about aspiration and relationships.”

	Bhardwaj added that every character and arc carried personal weight for him, since at some point in his own creative career he had stood where each of them stands. “The film explores the universal struggle to preserve our identities when our ambitions begin demanding that we sacrifice parts of ourselves. I want audiences to experience the same conflict our characters face – the tension between the relationships we value and the ambitions we choose to pursue.”
	

	Travelin Bone was set up by Marc Sternberg, Steve Garrow and Naresh Malik. Its Netflix original film “CTRL” preceded “The Method,” and the company is building out a film and TV slate aimed at both Indian and global viewers.

	“With ‘The Method,’ we are bringing together exceptional talent and creative teams from both countries,” said Garrow, the company’s co-founder and CEO. “It has been a wonderful experience working with Gaurav and witnessing the clarity and confidence with which he has approached his first feature film, particularly alongside an iconic actor like Harvey Keitel.”

	Garrow also credited Sundwall with real depth and presence on screen and said the two newcomers had delivered work beyond what he had expected.

	“‘The Method’ reflects the philosophy of my company in many ways,” said Lalit Bhatnagar, founder of Imagination Infinite Motion Pictures. “We are at a moment when content is becoming increasingly global – and so is talent. The traditional boundaries between industries and markets are becoming less relevant, creating an extraordinary opportunity to bring together artists from different backgrounds to tell compelling stories.”

schema.headline: Harvey Keitel Plays Acting Teacher in Gaurav Bhardwaj’s Debut Feature ‘The Method’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: La Oreja de Van Gogh Songs Set to Power an Ambitious Romantic Musical From Fernando González Molina (EXCLUSIVE)
description: The songs of pop group phenomenon La Oreja de Van Gogh, which has just become the only Spanish band with a song in Spotify’s Billions Club, are head
body:
The songs of pop group phenomenon La Oreja de Van Gogh, which has just become the only Spanish band with a song in Spotify’s Billions Club, are heading for the big screen, set to be sung and power the emotional currents of an ambitious romantic musical, “Puedes Contar Conmigo.”

	Director of blockbuster “Palm Trees in the Snow,” Fernando González Molina is on board to helm the movie. Preeminent Spanish producers Beltrán Cortázar, Domingo Corral and Gonzalo Sálazar-Simpson are set to produce. La Oreja de Van Gogh will also serve as executive producer on the film, which bids fair to become one of the biggest upcoming titles from Spain.
	

	“Seeing that our songs will gain a new life in cinema is a dream for us,” La Oreja de Van Gogh said in a statement. The movie project roles off its extensive 2026 comeback tour with Amaia Montero back as lead vocalist which staged over 100 concerts and sold more than 400,000 tickets to packed concerts across Spain, which confirmed the huge resilient across-generations fandom of the group. The group has over 50 Platinum and Gold Discs.


	“We’re at a beautiful moment at our career, feeling the affection of many, many people and we believe ‘Puedes Contar Conmigo’ will be a marvellous celebration of what unites us with our audience,” the band added.

	González Molina has had his biggest audience success with romantic dramas particularly 2010’s “Three Steps Above Heaven” (€9.9 million: $11.2 million), 2012’s I Want You” (€12.1 million: €13.6 million) and 2016’s “Palm Trees in the Snow,” a lush period piece which stood out for its scale, production values and spectacular visuals which grossed €17.1 million ($19.8 million) at the Spanish box office.
	

	Little is known about the musical’s plot, currently being written by González Molina and screenwriter Miguel López Martínez, save that it is an original story, will use La Oreja’s lyrics and is in an advanced stage of development and writing.

	The possibilities, however, are enormous given the longevity of La Oreja de Van Gogh – founded in 1996 – and its enormous repertoire. Also key is La Oreja d Van Gogh’s accessible style of broader audience pop-rock and surging choruses and above all the songs’ highly relatable emotions, whether nostalgia after break-up (“Los Rosas,” “La Playa”), fleeting fated love, (“Jueves”) and happiness at having lived a great romance (“El último vals”), to name just a few of the group’s greatest hits.

	The Ambition of ‘Puedes Contar Conmigo’

	Whatever the storyline line, the movie definitely looks set to be highly ambitious.

	“We’ve always told stories through our music and knowing that these stories will inspire such a big visual and narrative universe fills us with illusion,” the band said.

	“Translating the universe of the Oreja into an original story is a giant challenge for me,” González Molina added. “It’s also fulfilling a dream of updating big romantic musicals, which I have always loved, with the codes of contemporary cinema. With this film I’d love to make a cinema event that moves audiences like the songs of La Oreja de Van Gogh have done for decades.”

	“Being part of such a genuine mix of talent such as La Oreja de Van Gogh and Fernando is authentic luck for us,” said the producers. “We feel we have the bases of what could be a great film: Our challenge is to support them to make this dream as large as possible,” they added.

	A Pedigree Producer Package

	That ambition knits with the C.V. of its producers. Cortázar, for instance, is the former CEO of Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo’s Suma Content where his credits include Los Javis’ seven-part 2023 series “La Mesías,” a first instance of their full-on creativity, each episode with different genre influences, knit by a pop sensibility and varying formats across multiple timelines, all of which anticipated “La Bola Negra.”

	Founder of Lazona, Sálazar-Simpson is behind Goya Best Picture winner “No Rest for the Wicked,” and has produced two of the three highest-grossing Spanish films in Spain: 2014 comedy “Spanish Affair” (€56.2 million: $63.5 million) and Spanish Affair 2 (€36.1 million: $40.8 million).
	

	“Puedes contar conmigo” also stands out as the first movie announced by Domingo Corral, the former Head of Fiction and Entertainment at Movistar Plus, behind “La Mesías,” “Querer” and “Riot Police” in series and “Sirât,” “La Bola Negra,” “The Beloved” and “Sundays” in films.

	“As producers, we want to make a film that is different and unique and at the level of ambition which merit La Oreja de Van Gogh and their songs. Many are part of our emotional history across several generations and they have an enormous fan base in Latin America and the U.S. Hispanic,” said Corral, noting that one key reference is “La La Land.”

	“We are fortunate to have Fernando in,” he added. “We are convinced that his vision and passion will deliver a great film full of unforgettable emotional moments.”



	

					(L-R) Gonzalo Sálazar-Simpson, Fernando González Molina, Beltrán Gortázar, Domingo Corral @michaeloats

schema.headline: La Oreja de Van Gogh Songs Set to Power an Ambitious Romantic Musical From Fernando González Molina (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ITV Studios Travels to Mipcom With 10 New Titles on Its Formats Slate, Led by ‘The Chase Around the World’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: ITV Studios has unveiled 10 new titles on its Mipcom formats slate, led by “The Chase Around the World,” and also revealed the unscripted lineup, wh
body:
ITV Studios has unveiled 10 new titles on its Mipcom formats slate, led by “The Chase Around the World,” and also revealed the unscripted lineup, which includes “70 Up,” the final chapter of the groundbreaking documentary series “7 Up.”

	“The Chase Around the World,” a multi-country treasure hunt, is a spin-off of ITV’s game show “The Chase.” The series, comprising six hour-long episodes, is produced by Bright Entertainment for British broadcaster ITV.
	

	The show sees six pairs of contestants attempt to track down some of the biggest brains in Britain – six individuals known as The Chasers – in undisclosed locations across Europe. Unravelling puzzles along the way, the winning pair will pit their knowledge against The Chasers in order to win a life-changing prize pot.


	Also new to the slate is endurance experiment “Expedition Into the Wild.” The show had a very successful launch on Kanal 5 in Sweden, where it became the number 1 commercial title in its timeslot, outperforming the slot average by 60%, and has been commissioned for a second season. The show, which comprises 12 hour-long episodes, is produced by ITV Studios Sweden.

	In the show, eight celebrity city dwellers with almost no survival skills are dropped into a remote natural environment for 18 days. Working in pairs, the contestants have only basic tools and limited food. They must build shelter, source supplies and tackle survival challenges.

	“Celebrity Escape,” produced by Perpetual Entertainment for Three in New Zealand, sees seven comedians take on one of the most popular and fastest-growing activities in the world: the escape room.
	

	Each hour-long episode of the show sees the comedians working as a team to navigate the puzzles, clues and scares of a new themed room, before voting out their competition.

	All the while, another comedian, known as the Games Master, watches from the control room, chiming in to help or hinder as they see fit.

	Over the six episodes, alliances shift, egos clash, and pressure builds as the group shrinks. In the finale, the last two contestants face a head-to-head escape where only one can win.

	New food-entertainment series “Next on the Menu,” produced by South Shore for the U.K.’s Channel 4, sees four food superfans battle to create the next menu hit for a global brand, from Wagamama and KFC to Taco Bell and Krispy Kreme.

	Each contestant must pitch, prototype and perfect their dream dish with their creations then stress-tested for taste, kitchen feasibility, and trialled with real customers, to win a place on the menu. The show is in four parts, with each episode an hour long.

	Also new to the slate is “Apocalypse,” a new social experiment show from The Garden and ITV Studios Australia. It was the biggest unscripted original launch since 2024 for Binge, the Australian streaming service, and one of Channel 4’s biggest young-skewing entertainment launches of this year.

	The series, which has eight hour-long episodes, sees 16 ordinary people enter an abandoned town that bears all the hallmarks of being ravaged by an apocalyptic event. With no running water, heating or electricity, they must survive for 28 days, scavenging for food and supplies and by reusing and repurposing anything they find.

	“Secret Garden,” narrated by David Attenborough in the U.K., also joins the slate. The show, comprising five 60-minute episodes, is produced by Plimsoll Studios. It was the BBC’s biggest new factual series since 2025.

	The series uncovers the wildlife stories hidden in the places we know best. Each episode follows one garden over an extended period, capturing animal behavior rarely witnessed by human eyes – from raising families and defending territories to hunting, courting and surviving the changing seasons.

	Also on the slate is the reality format “How to Clean Up for Cash,” where loved ones secretly seek help for a family member or friend whose clutter has taken over their home.
	

	While the unsuspecting homeowner is away for 48 hours, an expert team clears, sorts and values years of accumulated belongings, transforming the space that has become overwhelmed by clutter.

	The six-parter, with each episode running for 30 minutes, is produced by MultiStory Media for ITV.

	“Name That Tune,” which is based on the U.S. game show that debuted on NBC in 1953, is returning to the U.K. in 2027 after 29 years off air.

	The show is a global staple of entertainment, with over 25 countries, including Australia, France, Germany and Italy, having produced localized versions across the last seven decades. Accompanied by the Name That Tune Live Band and led by a celebrity host, contestants race against the clock (and each other) to identify legendary tracks across various genres and eras.

	The series, comprising nine 60-minute episodes, is produced by Bright Entertainment for ITV.

	Also new to the slate is “The Ultimate Summer Star,” produced by Magga og Anders and ITV Studios Denmark for TV2 Echo. It is a sun-soaked spin-off of the smash-hit Norwegian format “The Ultimate Christmas Star,” which continues to deliver strong ratings with a 13% increase in total viewers from Season 2 to 3 in Norway, with a fourth season returning this December, a third season returning in Denmark, and a newly announced first season in Sweden.

	Chaos unfolds as 24 celebrities head to a lakeside cabin to compete in a lineup of bonkers challenges. From laugh-out-loud antics to outdoor adventures, the tasks are silly, light-hearted and packed with warm-weather fun, as they compete to be crowned The Ultimate Summer Star.

	The show has 24 30-minute episodes.

	And finally, there is “The Joy of Pets,” which is produced by Bandicoot for ITV. The show, which has five 60-minute episodes, is a warm-hearted factual entertainment format celebrating the bond between people and their animals.

	This format travels across the country uncovering uplifting, emotional and often surprising stories of pets, their owners and the veterinary professionals dedicated to their care.

	Each episode combines behind-the-scenes access to a local veterinary practice, a community roadshow featuring expert advice and audience interaction, and inspiring local stories that showcase the life-changing impact animals have on the people around them.
	



	

					“70 Up”
									Courtesy of ITV/Nick Wall
	



	ITV Studios has also unveiled its full unscripted slate for Mipcom, led by “70 Up,” the final chapter of the groundbreaking series “7 Up,” the longest-running documentary series ever made.

	“70 Up,” which comprises two 90-minute episodes, is produced by MultiStory Media for ITV.

	The “7 Up” series, which follows the lives of 14 ordinary people, has been broadcast in 157 countries, including the U.S., Canada, Japan, China, Australia and France.

	“70 Up” marks the culmination of this journey across seven decades. Building on the forensic questioning of the late director Michael Apted, Academy Award-winning filmmaker Asif Kapadia steps in to close the circle on a series that captures a lifetime from childhood through careers, marriage, parenting and beyond.

	From Plimsoll Studios for ITV, comes the landmark natural history series “World’s Wildest Cities.” Across six hour-long episodes, the show follows a variety of urban animals to uncover the challenges of living alongside the human race. Each episode has a new cast of animals and focuses on one city: Rio de Janeiro, New York, Melbourne, Singapore and London, with the final episode revealing how the series was made, and the science behind the stories.

	Another title looking at the changing world around us, “Ages of Ice,” which has three hour-long episodes, is produced by Northern Pictures for PBS and ABC Australia, and is narrated by actor David Tennant. It follows the brave scientists pushing the boundaries of exploration and human endeavor in Earth’s coldest corners to understand the changes of ice and what this means for our planet’s future. In the unforgiving grip of our planet’s polar regions, the series will follow these modern-day explorers as they try to understand how the fate of every place and every creature on our planet is tied to these frozen extremes.

	New to the slate from Wonderhood Studios is a documentary series “Jesus Christ: The Man, The Mystery,” which has four hour-long episodes. Produced for the BBC, it draws on the latest historical research, archaeological discoveries, technological innovation and expert testimony to expand and sharpen our understanding of Jesus.

	The story draws on the testimony recorded in the Gospel accounts, and elsewhere, to understand the world he inhabited and the foundations of the movement he inspired.
	

	And finally, from Curious Films, there is “Spy Next Door: The Anna Chapman Story,” which is produced for Channel 4. It has all the ingredients of an espionage thriller, but is a true story, with access to people caught up in the Russian spy network as well as FBI operatives and former Russian insiders.

	In 2010, 11 deep-cover Russian spies were arrested across the United States, sending shockwaves around the globe. At the center of it all was Anna Chapman (née Kushchenko) — the femme fatale turned media sensation. But before she became the face of the spy ring, she was recruited, trained and indoctrinated in the U.K. The series reveals how the actions of a few would trigger seismic, long-lasting and deadly consequences.

	It comprises two hour-long episodes.

	Variety spoke to Julie Meldal-Johnsen, executive VP global content and content strategy at ITV Studios, about the slate.

	Referring to “70 Up,” she said, “I can’t think of another documentary project that is more ambitious, more far-reaching. There were so few filmmakers that could have done it justice [following the death of Michael Apted], but it’s incredible to be able to wrap up that endeavor, that vision, and bring back some people who haven’t been in it for a long time. Obviously, sadly, there have been a couple of deaths on the way. It is a feat of filmmaking that will be unparalleled. So that brings tears to my eyes every time, and we’re really, really, really proud of that.”

	Turning her attention to “Jesus Christ: The Man, The Mystery,” she said, “It is very rare for us to have something in that space, but we were very keen. It’s a history documentary with archaeological discoveries thanks to new techniques, and some great expert testimony. We think this really will be a seminal documentary. And whether you’re Christian or not, I think it will be fascinating.”

	She added, “ ‘World’s Wildest Cities’ features a different city every episode, and there are some really exotic animals, and this amazing drama that takes place in urban places. It’s quite a different approach to blue chip natural history.”

	“Ages of Ice” has been three years in the making, she said. “We were excited to have it voiced by David Tennant, and the visuals on that are just stunning. It follows these polar-nauts to some of the most incredible and dangerous places on the planet, doing research to help us figure out how to manage water and changing climate.”
	

	Talking about “The Chase Around the World,” a spin-off of ITV’s game show “The Chase,” she said, “What I love about ‘The Chase’ is taking the quizzes and the studio show and getting it out into the world. We say The Chasers are both beloved and feared, and to see them out of their environment – of a safe, comfortable studio – and out into the world is great. Some of the locations are just gorgeous. The photography in the series is really great too, and it’s fun, and it’s getting that scale – these wonderful locations – and I think it’s just a clever way of wrapping up a treasure hunt and bit of travel porn in a way.”

	She also discussed “Spy Next Door: The Anna Chapman Story.” “I think there’s always a demand for stories about spies,” she said. “People are endlessly fascinated by spies, true or fictional, and it’s a remarkable story. And she was this glamorous woman, which just adds to the intrigue.”

title: John de Mol’s Formats Giant Talpa Studios Heads to Mipcom With New Shows ‘Sing With Me,’ ‘The Golden Elevators’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: John de Mol’s Talpa Studios, whose hit formats include quiz show “The Floor,” is heading to next week’s TV market Mipcom with a slate of new enterta
body:
John de Mol’s Talpa Studios, whose hit formats include quiz show “The Floor,” is heading to next week’s TV market Mipcom with a slate of new entertainment formats, led by “Sing With Me” and “The Golden Elevators.”

	“Sing With Me” is a feelgood music entertainment format developed in collaboration with Dutch producer IDTV, the creator of “The Traitors.” 

	In the show, aspiring singers get the chance to share the stage with some of the country’s biggest artists. Every performance begins as a solo, but when one of the established artists hears something special, they can grab a microphone and join in, transforming the performance into a duet. 
	

	The format launches on SBS6 in the Netherlands on Nov. 7.


	“The Golden Elevators,” a quiz show that combines general knowledge with social strategy, has been ordered by ITV in the U.K. and SBS6 in the Netherlands, where it is set to air early next year.

	Ten contestants enter a skyscraper where they must choose between two elevators, each representing a possible answer to 10 questions. Choose correctly and you go up; choose the wrong one and you’re out.

	Before the doors close, contestants may work together and share what they know – or deliberately send a rival into the wrong elevator – turning every question into a battle of knowledge, strategy and trust. Waiting at the top is a life-changing jackpot, to share with whoever makes it there.

	Talpa Studios continues to expand its global footprint, with 26 formats active across 34 countries, and Sebastian van Barneveld, Talpa Studios’ director of global distribution, underscores the role that partnerships play in that growth, alongside the company’s investment in original IP.
	

	Shows developed through partnerships now account for more than 40% of Talpa Studios’ catalog.

	“In a rapidly changing market, strong ideas need more than creativity alone. Collaboration and flexibility are key to making them travel,” he said. “Our Mipcom slate reflects that approach: by combining original IP with creative partnerships and developing formats that can work across markets, platforms and audiences, we’re creating multiple routes for ideas to grow.”

	The partnership model has delivered titles such as murder mystery format “A Party to Die For,” developed with ITV Studios, and “Let’s Play Ball,” originally co-developed by EndemolShine Nederland (part of Banijay Benelux), Talpa Studios and Signal.Stream. The format has since secured commissions in French Canada and Finland.

	Signal.Stream, a strategic partner for Talpa Studios, focused on creating formats for the streaming generation, has developed several other titles that are gaining traction in the market. “Most Wanted” has new commissions in Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Romania, while “Catch Us” has added new commissions from TV4 in Sweden and ProSieben in Germany, alongside adaptations in the Netherlands and Hungary.

	Talpa Studios’ established brands continue to build momentum around the world. “The Floor,” for example, has reached more than 30 territories. Meanwhile, “The Winner Takes It All” secured its first international sale to France Télévisions and a recommission in the Netherlands.

	Daily reality competition “The Alliance,” nominated for the Netherlands’ most prestigious television audience award, launched on Prime Video in India with a celebrity adaptation, and the streaming giant has confirmed a second season.

	“Caught in the Middle,” a high-energy studio game show in which a duo must outsmart 100 opponents closing in around them, is returning for a second season in the Netherlands and continues to travel internationally, with adaptations in Spain for Atresmedia and Australia for Seven Network.

	De Mol is a reality TV legend, who previously led Endemol and Talpa Media, the creators of such iconic brands as “Big Brother,” “Deal or No Deal,” “Fear Factor” and “The Voice.” Talpa Studios, formed in September 2023, is led by CEO Maarten Meijs.

            Streamer BenDaDonnn has been arrested after a chaotic video showed a police officer tasing him before placing him in cuffs ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            BenDaDonnn -- real name Benius Beard -- was booked into Brazos County Jail in Texas on a charge of evading arrest or detention Sunday.
      
    
      
      BenDaDonn was TASED and detained by police officers in Texas 😳 https://t.co/cBanBD16oL
              @KickStreamingHQ
          
  
    
            The College Station Police Department tells TMZ ... officers were working to clear patrons from the roadway in front of a bar when they encountered a group who refused to comply with their commands.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            When those lawful commands continued to be ignored, someone acting as BenDaDonn's security guard allegedly slapped an officer's hands out of the way as they were trying to detain BenDaDonnn ... according to police.
      
    
            The PIO claims the officer then deployed the taser -- calling it a less-lethal tool -- as BenDaDonnn was attempting to get away in order to gain compliance.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As the officer tried to take BenDaDonnn into custody ... his security guard allegedly pushed the officer before both were arrested.
      
    
            The man who police say claimed to be his security guard -- Kenny Carter -- was charged with Interference with Public Duties.
